notes: CardDemo's pending-authorization task (transaction CP00, program COPAUA0C, app-authorization-ims-db2-mq): the CKTI trigger monitor starts it with an MQTM naming the request queue; each comma-delimited request is decided against the account's summary segment (IMS DBPAUTP0, PSB PSBPAUTB) or, with none, ACCTDAT's limits, answered on the request's reply queue and recorded in IMS (the summary REPLaced, or INITIALIZEd REPLACING NUMERIC and ISRTed: register C17, then a PAUTDTL1 detail). The database is the corpus's own HD unload (22 roots, the last with a blank key left out: 21 seeded); the VSAM files are CardDemo's data plus two extra xref records. Both sides get the same queue manager, trigger data (register W3, W8) and database; every MQI call, EXEC DLI call and CICS command is an event compared with its completion codes, and the queues and final database bytes are compared. Derived from CardDemo (Apache-2.0; Copyright Amazon.com, Inc. or its affiliates): LICENSE and NOTICE here are the source's own. Not provable, by name: the request-limit exit (line 339, WS-MSG-PROCESSED > WS-REQSTS-PROCESS-LIMIT of 500, true outcome). WS-RESP-LENGTH (line 46, VALUE 1) is the STRING POINTER of every reply (line 730) and is never reset, so one task's replies accumulate in the 200-byte W02-PUT-BUFFER and the MQPUT1 length (line 756) is that pointer: three replies of 62 bytes fit, the fourth leaves the pointer at 201, a length one byte past the buffer, which IBM leaves undefined (storage beyond W02-PUT-BUFFER). Measured (#5278): three identical requests prove equal on both sides, four make the det port refuse the 201-byte read (IndexOutOfBounds) where GnuCOBOL reads the next byte of storage. No case can reach 501 requests without that read, so line 339 true stays an uncovered branch and no scenario states it.

scenarios.name: no-request
scenarios.why: the request queue is empty: MQGET 2033 ends the loop at once; no PSB is scheduled, nothing is replied

scenarios.name: approve-summary-found
scenarios.why: account 1 has a summary segment in DBPAUTP0 and funds left: reply 00 / 0000, the summary REPLaced and a PAUTDTL1 detail inserted under it

scenarios.name: schd-already-held
scenarios.why: DL/I fault: the first SCHD answers TC (the task already holds the PSB): 1200 TERMs and schedules again, and the request is then approved as in approve-summary-found

scenarios.name: decline-insufficient-funds
scenarios.why: account 17 (credit limit 568.00 in its summary): an amount over limit minus balance is declined 05 / 4100, still recorded (declined count and amount)

scenarios.name: approve-no-summary
scenarios.why: account 2 has no summary segment (GE): the limits come from ACCTDAT, the summary is INITIALIZEd REPLACING NUMERIC (register C17) and ISRTed, then the detail

scenarios.name: decline-no-summary-over-account-limit
scenarios.why: no summary and an amount over ACCT-CREDIT-LIMIT less ACCT-CURR-BAL: declined 4100 from the account's own figures

scenarios.name: card-not-in-xref
scenarios.why: READ CCXREF NOTFND: warning A001 to CSSL, declined 05 / 3100, and nothing is written to IMS

scenarios.name: account-not-in-master
scenarios.why: the xref names an account ACCTDAT does not hold: READ NOTFND logs A002, no summary exists, declined 3100

scenarios.name: customer-not-in-master
scenarios.why: the xref names a customer CUSTDAT does not hold: READ NOTFND logs A003; the account is found, so the decision is by funds

scenarios.name: same-account-twice
scenarios.why: two requests for an account with no summary: the first ISRTs it (C17 path), the second finds it and REPLaces it; a SYNCPOINT after each

scenarios.name: amount-without-decimals
scenarios.why: an amount with no decimal point or leading zeros goes through FUNCTION NUMVAL

scenarios.name: amount-with-sign
scenarios.why: a leading-plus amount, as PIC +9(10).99 prints it

scenarios.name: three-requests-mixed
scenarios.why: an approval, a decline and a card not in the xref in one task: the loop, SYNCPOINT and PSB re-schedule after each

scenarios.name: read-xref-io-error

faults.why: WHEN OTHER of 5100: the critical end routine

scenarios.why: READ CCXREF IOERR (WHEN OTHER): critical C001 to CSSL, then 9990-END-ROUTINE ends the task (TERM, MQCLOSE, RETURN)

scenarios.name: read-acct-io-error
scenarios.why: READ ACCTDAT IOERR: critical C002 and the end routine

scenarios.name: read-cust-io-error
scenarios.why: READ CUSTDAT IOERR: critical C003 and the end routine

scenarios.name: no-trigger-data
scenarios.why: RETRIEVE answers ENDDATA: the request queue name stays spaces, MQOPEN fails and the critical M001 ends the task

scenarios.name: no-reply-queue
scenarios.why: the reply queue is not defined: MQPUT1 fails (2085), critical M004 and the end routine; the request is already gone (MQGET NO_SYNCPOINT)

scenarios.name: gu-summary-bad-status
scenarios.why: DL/I fault: GU of the summary answers AC (not GE): WHEN OTHER of 5500, critical I002 and the end routine; nothing is replied or inserted

scenarios.name: repl-summary-fails
scenarios.why: DL/I fault: REPL of the found summary answers AC: 8400 sees a status that is not blank, critical I003 and the end routine

scenarios.name: request-longer-than-buffer
scenarios.why: MQGET of a 520-byte request into the 500-byte buffer, without ACCEPT-TRUNCATED-MSG: the call fails (CompCode 2, Reason 2080, MQRC_TRUNCATED_MSG_FAILED, not 2033), so 3100 logs critical M003 'FAILED TO READ REQUEST MQ' and the message stays on the queue

scenarios.name: schd-held-after-term
scenarios.why: DL/I fault: every SCHD answers TC (the task holds the PSB even after the TERM): 1200 TERMs, schedules again, STATUS-OK is false, so critical I001 'IMS SCHD FAILED'

scenarios.name: open-request-queue-fails
scenarios.why: MQ fault: the MQOPEN of the request queue answers 2009 (MQRC_CONNECTION_BROKEN, CompCode 2): critical M001 and the end routine; the request queue was never opened, so no MQCLOSE is made

scenarios.name: get-request-fails
scenarios.why: MQ fault: the first MQGET of the request queue answers 2009 (not 2033, which ends the loop quietly): critical M003 and the end routine, which closes the request queue; the request is left unread

scenarios.name: close-request-queue-fails
scenarios.why: MQ fault: the MQCLOSE of the request queue at 9100 answers 2009 (MQRC_CONNECTION_BROKEN, CompCode 2) after the request was approved as in approve-summary-found: warning M005 'FAILED TO CLOSE REQUEST MQ' (line 963 false), the task ends
